_h9.description: pattern: code with metavariables, $X one node, $$$ARGS zero or more ("foo($$$ARGS)"); a string is captured inside its quotes (import $$$ from "$S"); a qualified call a::foo(…) needs its own pattern; {context,selector} parses context and matches its selector-kind node, for a fragment that needs surrounding code. A declaration pattern (function, method, class, binding) requires what it spells and ignores the rest: "fn $N($$$) { $$$ }" also finds pub, async, generic and typed functions, "class $C { $M($$$) { $$$ } }" a class with that method among others. Parameters, a function body and spelled types stay exact; calls and expressions keep every part; a Java or C# method spells its type ("$T $M($$$) { $$$ }"). Exclude an unsaid part with not: {pattern:"fn $N($$$) { $$$ }",not:{has:{field:"return_type",regex:"."}}}. regex: tests a node's whole text, so alone it also matches every enclosing node up to the file; pair it with kind or field: {kind:"impl_item",has:{field:"trait",regex:"^Name$"}}. kind: as syntaxTree prints it; Rust macro bodies are parsed as code, so x.y() there holds a field_identifier, not a token. has, inside: direct children, direct parent; stopBy:"end" reaches any depth: {kind:"class_declaration",has:{kind:"return_statement",stopBy:"end"}}. field (has, inside only): a grammar field. all, any, not: combine rules. nthChild: 1-based among named siblings, an integer or An+B. range: 0-based line and column.
